raw_response:
I farm only 6 mu, so I will keep the wheat-maize rotation on all of it instead of changing crops. That fits my land, my experience, and my well irrigation. At my age and with some family labor working off-farm, I will choose a steady, familiar plan that does not need too much extra field work but still aims for reliable yield. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put most fertilizer up front with a moderate total rate, irrigate at key stages, and keep pesticide use limited to what is needed for common diseases and insects. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want stronger yield on small land, apply enough nitrogen to support growth, use fewer irrigations than wheat because I have the wheat-maize system and must manage labor carefully, and keep tillage simple with rotary tillage. I will not chase the highest possible input level; I will aim for stable production, manageable cost, and lower labor pressure while using the well when the crop most needs water.
